### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes (strong)
- **If yes, what kind?** Manuscripts must demonstrate **experimental social-psychology contribution** meeting JESP's 10-Item Submission Checklist (community evidence: JESP 2022 — a priori power analysis, sample size determination, full reporting of all statistics).
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: Manuscripts failing checklist face desk rejection. IF 2024: 3.99 (community evidence: editage 2026-05). ~150 articles per year, 6 issues.

## Strategic Notes

### Hard Blockers

- Failure to meet JESP's 10-Item Checklist (community evidence: JESP 2022 + ScienceDirect 2026-05)
- Underpowered designs without a priori power analysis
- AI-generated images per Elsevier policy
- Failure to disclose AI use

### Soft Tax

Moderate. 10-Item Checklist compliance demands careful preregistration / power planning before submission. 24-month AAM embargo on subscription path.

### Best Suited For

- Experimental social psychology with strong design rigor
- Replication studies and registered reports
- Attitude change, social cognition, group dynamics empirical work
- Prejudice / stereotyping experiments
- Preregistered theory-test research

### Not Recommended For

- Pure correlational survey work without experimental component
- Underpowered or pilot studies
- Pure qualitative submissions
- Authors unfamiliar with current open-science practices

### Rejection Fallback Chain

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | [Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin](./personality-and-social-psychology-bulletin.md) | SPSP-affiliated; SAGE; comparable empirical paradigm |
| 2 | [Journal of Applied Social Psychology](./journal-of-applied-social-psychology.md) | If applied-social angle |
| 3 | [European Journal of Social Psychology](./european-journal-of-social-psychology.md) | EASP-affiliated; European social-psychology |

**Reverse direction** *(optional)*: If your paper was rejected from JPSP as "too narrowly experimental," JESP is often a better fit — specializes in experimental social-psychology rigor with open-science checklist culture.
